thread:
sam: Hey team — opened a PR to add a GPU node pool for experiment workloads: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/842. Key questions: how do we want capacity reservations vs spot fallback, IAM for driver install, and autoscaler tagging. Paste of the terraform plan and proposed module vars below. Please review.

devops-bot: terraform plan output: +1 aws_eks_node_group.gpu, +1 aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.gpu-driver, no deletes. Plan file: https://ci.redwood.dev/plan/842

sam: Relevant tf snippet I prototyped in the module: 
```
module "gpu_node_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/gpu-nodepool.git//aws"
  instance_type = "g5.2xlarge"
  desired_capacity = 4
  spot = true
  spot_fallback = true
  taints = ["nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule"]
  labels = { "gpu" = "true" }
}
```

jin: Quick thought — we should probably split guaranteed capacity and spot burst into two pools for predictability. Keep a small on-demand pool pinned for Dedicated jobs (1-2 nodes) and a larger spot pool for experiments. AWS capacity reservations are possible but messy; two node groups is simpler and clearer for scheduling.

maria: Agree with split. If we go ASG/mixed instances path, set `on_demand_base_capacity = 1` and `on_demand_percentage_above_base = 10` (or use an explicit on-demand pool for guaranteed). Also recommend `instance_types = ["g5.2xlarge","g4dn.xlarge"]` (mixed policy) to reduce interruption risk. In terraform for eks_node_group, prefer `capacity_type = var.use_spot ? "SPOT" : "ON_DEMAND"` rather than a boolean flag named `spot`.

maria: TF example: 
```
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu" {
  node_group_name = "gpu-pool"
  cluster_name    = var.cluster_name
  instance_types  = var.instance_types
  capacity_type   = var.use_spot ? "SPOT" : "ON_DEMAND"
  scaling_config { desired_size = var.desired_capacity; max_size = var.max_capacity; min_size = var.min_capacity }
  launch_template { id = aws_launch_template.gpu.id }
}
```

luis: One more infra-y piece — the GPU bootstrap script pulls drivers from a private S3 bucket and reads the driver version from SSM. Make sure the node IAM role gets s3:GetObject on `redwood-gpu-drivers/*` and ssm:GetParameter on `/drivers/nvidia/*`. I added a draft iam policy in the module but want someone to sanity-check names/attachments.

luis: IAM snippet I added: 
```
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "gpu_driver_access" {
  name = "gpu-driver-access"
  role = aws_iam_role.node_role.name
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17",
    Statement = [
      {Action = ["s3:GetObject"], Resource = "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-gpu-drivers/*", Effect = "Allow"},
      {Action = ["ssm:GetParameter"], Resource = "arn:aws:ssm:*:*:parameter/drivers/nvidia/*", Effect = "Allow"}
    ]
  })
}
```

sam: Good catch. Jin — can you add the separate on-demand pool config in the PR (small pool with taint `capacity=guaranteed` and matching tolerations)? Maria — can you rename `spot` -> `use_spot` and add `instance_types` var + doc string?

jin: Will do. On the k8s side I'll add label `gpu=true` and toleration for `nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule`. Also set kubelet `--max-pods` lower on GPU nodes to avoid ENI exhaustion for dense workloads. Toleration example: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-test
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeSelector:
    gpu: "true"
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: ubuntu
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```

maria: nit: rename var `spot_fallback` -> `allow_spot_fallback` and document behavior (fallback to on-demand ASG or spin up ondemand pool). Also add autoscaler tags on the ASG/nodegroup: `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled = true` and `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/${cluster_name} = owned`. Without tags CA won't touch spot nodes.

devops-bot: CI: terraform plan succeeded for PR #842. Summary: +1 aws_eks_node_group.gpu, +1 aws_iam_role_policy.gpu_driver_access. Plan link: https://ci.redwood.dev/plan/842#summary

sam: If no objections I'll merge after jin/maria update vars and once CI passes. Also please ensure we add an entry to CHANGELOG and document the node pool's purpose in the infra README so SRE knows to update oncall runbooks (driver issues).

maria: :thumbsup: I'll push the var rename and autoscaler tags change in a follow-up commit.

sam: Thanks all — once apply completes I'll spin up a smoke job to verify driver installation and a small ML workload to validate throughput.
